title: Cross-hand trial-order covariance did not improve cross-cycle prediction of grasping difficulty
abstract: In separately sampled NHANES 2011–2012 to 2013–2014 adults aged at least 60, adding cross-hand trial-order covariance did not establish better grasping-difficulty prediction beyond strength, asymmetry, marginal variability, demographics, BMI and pain: weighted Brier delta -0.000048708, target PSU 95% interval [-0.000960449, +0.000887775], joint-refit interval [-0.001320904, +0.001446336]. Frozen development and confirmation included 1,429 and 1,527 complete-case older adults. AUC and log loss worsened; author checks, uncertainty and code accompany this scoped negative result.
